sources.entry: opencv-python - Open Source Computer Vision Library.

summary.one_liner: Pre-built pip wheels of OpenCV's Python bindings (CPU-only), available as main, headless, and contrib variants, plus scripts for building them from source.
summary.what_it_does:
This repository packages OpenCV's Python bindings as pip-installable wheels, so users can run pip install and then import cv2 without a separate OpenCV installation. It offers four packages: main modules, full contrib/extra modules, and headless variants of each for servers and containers without GUI libraries. The README lists supported Python versions (3.7 through 3.14) and says the wheels are CPU-only. It explains that the build is driven by a setup.py and CI matrix that uses environment variables such as ENABLE_CONTRIB, ENABLE_HEADLESS, and CMAKE_ARGS to customize builds. It also covers manual builds, debug builds, and source distributions for platforms without a matching wheel. The README includes an FAQ on common Windows DLL import errors, pip version requirements, and why non-free algorithms such as SURF are excluded while SIFT is included.</what_it_does>
<use_cases>["install OpenCV for Python with pip", "run image processing in Docker or cloud servers without a GUI", "face detection with Haar cascades", "build a custom OpenCV wheel with extra modules like CUDA", "troubleshoot OpenCV import errors on Windows", "use OpenCV contrib modules from Python"]</use_cases>
<how_to_run">["pip install --upgrade pip", "pip install opencv-python", "pip install opencv-contrib-python-headless  # headless server variant with contrib modules", "import cv2", "git clone --recursive <repo-url> && cd opencv-python", "pip wheel . --verbose  # manual build"]</how_to_run>
<stack">["Python", "OpenCV (C++ core and bindings)", "pip / PyPI wheels", "CMake", "scikit-build", "NumPy", "manylinux2014 Docker images", "auditwheel", "delocate", "GitHub Actions"]</stack>
<notable">["Four package variants (main, contrib, headless main, headless contrib) so server images can skip X11/Qt dependencies", "Haar cascade XML files are bundled and accessible via cv2.data.haarcascades", "Source distributions on PyPI let pip build OpenCV when no wheel matches the platform", "SIFT is included because its patent expired, while SURF is excluded as non-free", "Only one of the four packages should be installed per environment because they share the cv2 namespace"]</notable>
<caveats">["Wheels are CPU-only; CUDA and other extra dependencies require a manual build from source", "This repo contains only packaging scripts; bugs in OpenCV functions should be reported to the upstream OpenCV project", "Windows import errors may need Visual C++ redistributable or Media Feature Pack; old pip versions (below 19.3) fail to install the wheels"]</caveats>
